sections.h2: Which two courthouse offices deal with Henry County property tax?
sections.html:
Both sit at 100 West Franklin in Clinton, ZIP 64735. Scott Largent is the assessor, reachable at 660-885-7212. His page keeps early hours, 7:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Monday to Friday, and offers weekend or evening visits by appointment. The county also publishes a GIS mapping link from the same page.

Bills come from a different desk. The state's collector directory lists the Henry County Treasurer as Ex Officio Collector of Revenue, with phone 660-885-7207, fax 660-885-7259 and email collector@henrycountymo.net. Questions about a value belong with the assessor. Questions about a balance belong with the collector.

sections.h2: What does Henry County look like on the ground?
sections.html:
Henry County sits in west-central Missouri and touches Johnson, Pettis, Benton, St. Clair, Bates and Cass counties. Its land area is 697 square miles, and another 35 square miles is water. It began in December 1834 as Rives County and took the name Henry in 1841, honoring Patrick Henry.

The county's own history page calls agriculture the economic base and says about 80 percent of the county is forested, hilly ground, much of it beside federal land around the 55,600 acre Harry S. Truman Reservoir. Hunters and anglers are a steady presence. State routes 7, 13, 18 and 52 are the main roads, and Jefferson Lines provides intercity bus service.

Clinton, the seat, is the largest town at an estimated 8,945 people. Windsor follows with 2,847, then Urich (492), Calhoun (455), Deepwater (422) and Montrose (375). Blairstown, Brownington and Tightwad have fewer than 100 residents each.

sections.h2: How did Clinton become the seat of Henry County, and what is the courthouse like?
sections.html:
The county site says the first hunters and trappers came through in 1826 and the first settlers arrived in the fall of 1830. In 1836 the site for the seat was chosen and named for DeWitt Clinton, then a New York governor. The first court session met in a home on May 4, 1835.

The first courthouse dates to 1837 and was condemned in 1884, then taken down in 1887. Voters approved a $50,000 bond in 1891, and the contract for the present courthouse went to D. J. Hyde and Company of Sedalia for $47,221 in February 1892. Its cornerstone was laid on June 24, 1892.

sections.h2: What outdoor features affect how Henry County properties are marketed?
sections.html: The county calls itself a sportsman's paradise. It lists many species of fish in local waters, hunting for deer, coyote, squirrel, turkey and dove, and migratory waterfowl on the Truman Reservoir. A parcel near the shoreline, or one with timber and creek frontage, will be described differently from a town lot in Clinton or Windsor, and the assessor's classification can differ too, since farm and residential ground carry different assessment rates.

sections.h2: Which school districts and libraries serve Henry County homes?
sections.html:
Buyers of a Henry County house usually ask which district it falls in, and the assessor's parcel record answers that. Districts anchored in the county include:

  • Clinton School District, with an early childhood center, Henry Elementary, Clinton Intermediate, Clinton Middle and Clinton High
  • Henry County R-1 in Windsor
  • Calhoun R-VIII, Montrose R-XIV, Davis R-XII, Leesville R-IX and Shawnee R-III
  • Lakeland R-III, which serves Deepwater and Lowry City and is physically in St. Clair County

Private options include Holy Rosary Catholic School in Clinton, St. Mary's School in Montrose and the Windsor Amish Schools. The Henry County Library and its Lenora Blackmore Branch serve the public.

sections.h2: How does Missouri set the taxable value of a Henry County house?
sections.html:
The assessor applies a fixed share of market value: 19 percent for homes, 12 percent for farmland, 32 percent for commercial property, according to RSMo 137.115. Fresh values go on the books in odd-numbered years and hold through the even year that follows.

  • A jump of more than 15 percent on a home, apart from new construction, triggers an on-site inspection.
  • The owner is told in writing and has 30 days or more to request a look inside.
  • A drive-by does not satisfy the statute.

If such a jump is appealed, RSMo 138.060 puts the burden on the assessor to show the value is no higher than market value.

sections.h2: How can a Henry County owner challenge a value?
sections.html:
The first stop is the county Board of Equalization, with a filing cutoff the State Tax Commission gives as the second Monday in July. A ruling against you can go to the Commission, which allows 30 days from the date of the Board's letter. Filing is online, by email to Legal@stc.mo.gov or by post to PO Box 146, Jefferson City, MO 65102-0146.

Property held by a company, trust or estate needs a lawyer to file. Your complaint should carry the tax bill or the Board's letter, and nothing else at first. An agreed value signed with the assessor closes the door on further appeal. Call 660-885-7212 for the local forms.

sections.h2: What dates matter on a Henry County tax calendar?
sections.html:
Missouri taxes whoever holds the property on January 1. A Henry County owner or seller should watch these dates:

  • January 1: assessment date
  • Odd years: new real estate values
  • Second Monday in July: Board of Equalization filing cutoff
  • December 31: bill due, with mailed payments judged by postmark under RSMo 139.100
  • After January 1: penalty added by the collector
  • Fourth Monday in August: sale of delinquent land

Call the collector for this year's mailing date and the penalty figure.

sections.h2: What if my Henry County house has back taxes when I sell?
sections.html:
Missouri lets the county sell delinquent land on the fourth Monday of August, and RSMo 140.150 lets the owner stop the sale by paying tax, penalty, interest and costs to the collector first. Notice goes by first class mail to the recorded owner, and a letter that never shows up cancels nothing.

Request a payoff from 660-885-7207 before you list, then hand the figure to your title company. If you dispute the value, RSMo 139.031 allows payment under protest: full payment before delinquency, a written statement to the collector, and a circuit court suit within ninety days.

faqs.q: Who prints the Henry County property tax bill?
faqs.a: The Treasurer, acting as Ex Officio Collector of Revenue, at 100 West Franklin in Clinton. The state directory lists 660-885-7207 for that office.

faqs.q: Which percentage applies to a Henry County residence?
faqs.a: Nineteen percent of true value. Farmland is assessed at 12 percent and commercial property at 32 percent, and the local levy then applies to the assessed figure.

faqs.q: Is there a grace period after December 31 in Henry County?
faqs.a: Missouri judges mailed payments by postmark, and the collector adds a penalty once January 1 arrives. Ask the collector's office whether any exception applies to you.

faqs.q: Could Henry County auction my home over unpaid tax?
faqs.a: Yes, the statute allows a sale of delinquent land on the fourth Monday of August. Paying the tax, penalty, interest and costs to the collector before then stops the sale.

faqs.q: How do I reach the Henry County assessor?
faqs.a: Phone 660-885-7212 or stop by 100 West Franklin in Clinton. Weekday hours are 7:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., and appointments outside those hours are available.
